newsitem.title: UK: Betjeman honoured among British literary greats.
newsitem.headline: Betjeman honoured among British literary greats.

text.p: A stone tablet dedicated to the late poet laureate Sir John Betjeman was unveiled in Poet's Corner in Westminster Abbey on Monday to honour him with a place among the greats of English literature.

Betjeman, who died in 1984, joined literary figures such as Shakespeare, Byron, Keats, Chaucer and Wordsworth in the famous corner of the London abbey, where British monarchs, including Queen Elizabeth, have been crowned.
Some of the poet's works, including "Old Friends, Seaside Golf", "Summoned By Bells" and "In A Bath Tea Shop", were read at the ceremony.
"I'm sure he would have loved tonight. He was a very kind and loving man who enjoyed laughter," said Betjeman's granddaughter Lucy Ward, who used to read him poetry in his later years.
